# ctables/binop

> Helper: evaluates both operands of a binary operator into temporaries.

truck [ctables](../ctables.md) · [source](../../../registry/ctables/binop.pkg)

  Included by the operator packages with `@binop`. It opens a GCC
  statement expression and declares `{L.a}` (the left operand) and `{L.b}`
  (the right one), in that order; the operator adds the result and closes
  it with `})`. Declaring them as statements fixes the order of evaluation,
  which plain C leaves open, so side effects happen in the same order as
  with bintables. `cc -O2` keeps both in registers.

## Emit variants

The first variant whose condition holds is used.

### `emit`

```nasm
({ W {L.a} =
{left}
; W {L.b} =
{right}
;
```
